post.summary: Say that this client is leaving
post.description: A hint, never a command. A daemon started with `--idle-exit` normally waits out its whole idle period after the last client has gone; after this request it waits only a few seconds (3), and only while nothing else happens. Running work, an open event stream, a new connection or any other request keeps it running, so another client is never cut off by one client leaving. A daemon without `--idle-exit`, such as the systemd service, ignores it. There is no request body, and nothing is returned beyond acknowledgement. Clients call it best-effort as they close; a client that crashes simply never does, and the daemon then falls back to its idle period.

post.summary: Find, and optionally fix, cards hidden under missing or trashed parents
post.description: A live card whose parent is missing or trashed cannot be reached by browsing from the project's top level. This can happen after an older client trashed a parent, a card file was removed by hand, or a sync brought either in. Without apply, this only reports, reading the database alone (so it works on a locked encrypted project). With apply, each hidden branch moves to its nearest live, reachable ancestor (or the top level), into the place its trashed ancestor held, with its descendants still attached, in one commit. Applying twice changes nothing the second time. Cards in parent cycles are reported and left alone. The daemon also repairs at startup and core repairs after every pull.
